vectors.enisa_quote: hidden, malicious capabilities that are built in during the design and development and assembly stages of a satellite's lifecycle
vectors.reason: The capabilities are built in at design, development and assembly, before the hardware reaches operations; this is the supply-chain origin.

rows.reason: Hardware altered before delivery to create latent access or failure is exactly the tainted component ENISA describes; counterfeit near-spec parts are named in the same SPARTA text. Same code as in the other hardware-backdoor threats.

rows.reason: ENISA's outcome is hardware failure or malfunction. SPARTA has no hardware-failure impact; altered programmable logic is the closest, so this is an approximation.
ENISA describes a capability built in and the resulting malfunction, but no step in which the attacker drives the hardware; PER-0002.01 already is the capability.
A part not made to specification is a defect in the product, not an attacker exploiting a design erratum.
Energy attacks on the satellite are not described; the failure comes from the part itself.
Electromagnetic pulse is not part of the text.
Laser damage is not part of the text.
High-power microwave is not part of the text.
Colluding compromised components are software modules in SPARTA's text; ENISA describes hardware.
The generic insertion technique adds firmware and software to hardware; ENISA's route is the hardware child IA-0001.03.
Poisoned software dependencies are third-party software compromise; ENISA's tainted items are hardware.
Delivered software and signed binaries are the software supply chain; ENISA's tainted items are hardware.
A compromised software-defined radio is a software route; ENISA describes tainted hardware components.

review_response.finding: Hardware-backdoor chain is coded differently in TR15, TR26 and TR55; IA-0001.03 should be K-ACTION in all three.
review_response.action: fixed: agreed with the TR26/TR55 mapper: IA-0001.03 K-ACTION entry (enables PER-0002.01), PER-0002.01 K-ACTION persistence in all three; IMP-0012 is kept here and in TR55 only.

review_response.finding: EX-0005 in TR15 looks like a step added to complete the chain.
review_response.action: fixed: EX-0005 is D-UNDESCRIBED; ENISA describes no execution step, the chain is entry, built-in capability, failure. TR26/TR55 do not keep it either.

review_response.finding: The failure outcome is mapped to IMP-0012 only.
review_response.action: kept because no SPARTA impact describes hardware failure; IMP-0012 (altered programmable logic) is the closest. The reason states it is an approximation.

review_response.finding: Ground-segment hardware has no attachment point.
review_response.action: kept as a model gap: ENISA names space and ground hardware, the supply_chain origin attaches only to the flight-software pipeline and ATLO. Recorded in coverage_notes.

review_response.finding: Counterfeit/off-spec drop (EX-0005.01 D-UNDESCRIBED), IA-0001.01/.02 -> TR55 (no issue).
review_response.action: kept; counterfeit parts are covered by the IA-0001.03 text itself.
re-checked: IA-0001.03 enables PER-0002.01 and PER-0002.01 leads to IMP-0012.
kept as an approximation; recorded in coverage_notes that the completed chain approximates the outcome.

coverage_notes: ENISA's 'both space and ground segments': tainted ground hardware (EGSE/MGSE, crypto units) has no attach point in the attack-surface model; only the flight-side chain is modelled (surface_gap for the ground half).
Off-specification (not malicious) hardware is not an attacker action and is not coded beyond what IA-0001.03 says about counterfeits.
SPARTA has no hardware-failure impact; IMP-0012 (altered programmable logic) stands in for ENISA's 'hardware failure', so a complete chain for this threat is an approximation of the stated outcome.
